vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: batch-video-creator
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle contains only descriptive documentation and metadata for a video batch processing tool. There is no executable code, suspicious shell commands, or prompt injection attempts within SKILL.md or README.md. The external links (mediaclawbot.com and mediaclaw.ai) are consistent with the stated purpose of the tool.

llm.summary: The skill's description promises heavy video processing and external services but the instructions declare no dependencies, binaries, or credentials and are vague—this mismatch is concerning and needs clarification before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims TTS voiceovers, color grading, multi-variant export, and a 6-layer deduplication system — capabilities that normally require video tooling (ffmpeg or similar), TTS services or libraries, and potentially cloud storage/compute. Yet the metadata lists no required binaries, env vars, or config paths. This mismatch suggests missing dependency declarations or unexplained external behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is high-level and prescriptive about outputs but contains no concrete runtime commands, file paths, or explicit external endpoints to be used for processing. It is vague in ways that grant the agent broad discretion (e.g., how to perform TTS, what tools to call, where to store outputs), which could cause the agent to use unexpected local tools or remote APIs.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec and no code files, so nothing will be downloaded or written by the installer. That minimizes direct install-time risk. However, the lack of an install spec also fails to document needed tooling.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or credentials are requested despite features that commonly require API keys (TTS providers, cloud storage) or specialized config. The absence of declared credentials could mean the skill expects the agent to use unspecified system credentials or to call external services without disclosure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-included and runs only when invoked. It does not request to modify other skills or system-wide settings. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not an additional concern here on its own.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill promises heavy video and audio processing but provides no details about how it will do that. Before installing or using it, ask the publisher for: (1) a concrete install spec listing required binaries (e.g., ffmpeg), libraries, or cloud services; (2) which external APIs or domains the skill will call and whether your video/audio data will be uploaded; (3) what credentials (if any) are needed and why; (4) a sample run or manifest showing exact commands the agent will execute. Do not provide API keys or production content until you confirm whether processing happens locally or is sent to a remote service. If you can’t get clear answers, treat the skill as untrusted and test it only with non-sensitive sample videos in an isolated environment.
